headline.text: A very strong El Niño is under way, close to the 1997–98 record. It should peak around December, and its effects on rain, drought and heat will last into mid-2027.

zones.name: Northeast Argentina (Litoral)
zones.now: The Paraná and Uruguay rivers are in flood. Two people died in Corrientes on 19 October and families have been evacuated in Corrientes, Entre Ríos and Chaco. The Iguazú is running at ten times its normal flow.

next.text: The Uruguay River at Concordia is forecast to pass its 12.5 m evacuation level. Rain stays above normal, with up to 260 mm in intense episodes.
The Paraná at Corrientes is forecast to peak near 6 m, half a metre below the alert level.
In past strong El Niños the worst floods came in late summer and autumn, once the ground was already soaked.

prepare: Know your evacuation route and the nearest shelter.
Keep documents, medicines and a charged phone in a waterproof bag.
Never cross a flooded street or river, on foot or by car.
Follow river and storm alerts from the official sources below.
If you keep livestock or stock near the river, move it to higher ground early.

zones.name: Buenos Aires and the Pampas
zones.now: Soils in Buenos Aires province are about 95% saturated, so heavy rain quickly floods fields and rural roads.

next.text: 30–70% chance of more rain than normal, especially in western Buenos Aires province.
Strong storms are likely. In Greater Buenos Aires, street flooding will depend on how intense each storm is and how drains cope.

prepare: Clear gutters and drains before storms.
Follow storm alerts from the SMN.
In rural areas, plan around waterlogged roads.
Wetter soils are good news for most crops this season.

zones.name: Northern Patagonia
zones.now: Among the highest odds in the country of more rain than normal this season.

next.text: Above-normal rain likely. Watch for local flooding in valleys.

prepare: Save water and keep a few days of drinking water in case of supply cuts.
Avoid any open burning and report fires early.
On very hot days, avoid outdoor effort between 11:00 and 16:00 and drink water often.
Follow drought and water-supply notices from the official sources below.

zones.name: Uruguay River coast

prepare: Check the air-quality index before going out.

Children, older people and anyone with asthma or heart problems should take extra care.
Avoid any open burning and report fires early.
Low rivers can cut boat transport and supplies; plan ahead.

alerts.text: Watershed rain 34% below average. National emergency declared; further cuts possible.

alerts.title: Drought red alert in 103 municipalities
alerts.text: 233 of 298 municipalities under some drought alert. Severe crop losses and water shortages.

alerts.title: National red alert for drought
alerts.text: Harvests and day-labour income hit hardest, according to Oxfam.

alerts.title: Crop losses and poor water access
alerts.text: Among the most severe impacts in the region, alongside Honduras.

alerts.title: Months-long peat fires spread haze
alerts.text: Fires in Borneo and South Sumatra; over 200,000 hectares burned. Tens of thousands of people ill.

alerts.title: Peatland fires in South Sumatra
alerts.text: Drained peat and dry weather keep fires burning.

alerts.title: Over 60 days without rain in 25 provinces
alerts.text: Longest dry spell: 131 days in Bantul. Rainy season delayed across 61% of the country.

alerts.title: Schools closed because of haze
alerts.text: Emergency declared in Sarawak in September; asthma cases up 259% in late August.

alerts.title: Subsidies for haze-related illness
alerts.text: The government covers treatment costs as smoke drifts in.

alerts.title: Every province expected in drought by March
alerts.text: Rainfall 40–80% below normal through May. The government is preparing for power strain and lower hydropower.

alerts.title: Unseasonal heat and power cuts
alerts.text: Warnings of outages, drought and drinking-water shortages.

alerts.title: Fill reservoirs now, authorities urge
alerts.text: Rainy-season rainfall 20–40% below normal; saltwater intrusion expected Feb–Apr 2027.

timeline.title: El Niño declared
timeline.text: US forecasters (NOAA) confirm El Niño has formed in the Pacific.

timeline.title: Drought alerts in Central America
timeline.text: Honduras and El Salvador issue red alerts for drought.

timeline.title: Ecuador: national red alert
timeline.text: Weeks of rain on the coast trigger the national alert.

timeline.title: Haze emergency in Sarawak
timeline.text: Smoke from Indonesian fires; top-level regional haze alert.

timeline.title: Panama Canal cuts traffic
timeline.text: Daily transits cut to 32 as reservoirs run low.

timeline.title: Deadly floods in Corrientes
timeline.text: The Paraná and Uruguay rivers flood; evacuations in Argentina and Paraguay.

timeline.title: Heaviest rain on Ecuador's coast
timeline.text: INAMHI expects the most intense rain in Nov–Dec.

timeline.title: Extreme rain starts in northern Peru
timeline.text: 250–300 mm expected where 20–30 mm is normal.

timeline.title: Indonesia's rains arrive
timeline.text: Late rainy season should end the fires; watch for floods.

timeline.title: El Niño peaks
timeline.text: Strongest point expected between November and January.

timeline.title: Colombia's driest stretch
timeline.text: Worst rain deficit and highest risk of water rationing.

timeline.title: Panama dry season
timeline.text: Possible further canal cuts and water restrictions.

timeline.title: Worst flood season in Argentina's Litoral
timeline.text: Jan–Apr is when past strong El Niños caused the biggest floods.

timeline.title: Salt water in the Mekong Delta
Drought across the Philippines
timeline.text: Every province expected to be dry or in drought.

timeline.title: Extreme heat in Southeast Asia
timeline.text: Heat index up to 52–55 °C in the Philippines; 40 °C in Malaysia.
